hints: Focus on the shape as well as the position of the absorptions, a broad dip tells you a lot about hydrogen bonding.
Notice the strong, broad absorption centred around 3300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and check whether there is a strong sharp dip around 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ for $\text{C=O}$.
Compare a fairly neat alcohol $\text{O-H}$ above 3200 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ with no carbonyl against the very broad acid $\text{O-H}$ plus carbonyl pattern to pick the match.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two most important regions**

Look first at 3200 to 3600 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and at 1680 to 1750 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. These tell you about $\text{O-H}$ and $\text{C=O}$ groups.

Key IR guide:
$$\text{O-H (alcohol): broad, 3200-3600 cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{C=O: strong sharp, about 1700-1750 cm}^{-1}$$

**Read spectrum P**

Spectrum P has a clear broad absorption with low transmittance centred near 3350 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. That is classic hydrogen bonded $\text{O-H}$.

There are also sharp dips just below 3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ for $\text{C-H}$, but there is no strong sharp dip around 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ where a $\text{C=O}$ would appear.

**Match to the functional group**

No $\text{C=O}$ means it cannot be an ester, aldehyde or carboxylic acid. It must be an alcohol.

The broad $\text{O-H}$ above 3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ without the extra very broad 2500 to 3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ tail of an acid fits propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$.

options.A: Methyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3$, is an ester. It has a strong $\text{C=O}$ absorption near 1740 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and no $\text{O-H}$ absorption. Spectrum P has a broad $\text{O-H}$ and no carbonyl, so this is ruled out.
options.B: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde. It should show a strong $\text{C=O}$ near 1720 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ plus aldehyde $\text{C-H}$ near 2720 and 2820 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, and no broad $\text{O-H}$. Spectrum P shows the opposite pattern.
options.C: Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, has both $\text{C=O}$ near 1710 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and a very broad $\text{O-H}$ stretching from about 2500 to 3300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ that overlaps the $\text{C-H}$ region. Spectrum P lacks the carbonyl dip and its broad $\text{O-H}$ is neater and centred higher, so it is not an acid.
options.D: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol. It gives a broad hydrogen bonded $\text{O-H}$ absorption around 3200 to 3600 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, $\text{C-H}$ absorptions just below 3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, and no $\text{C=O}$ absorption. This matches spectrum P exactly.
